newsitem.title: PERU: Peru loses 461,720 man-hours in strikes in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Peru loses 461,720 man-hours in strikes in Sept.

text.p: Peru lost 461,720 man-hours in six private sector strikes during September, up from the 38,400 man-hours lost during three strikes in the same month last year, the Labor Ministry said Thursday.

The main reason for the large jump in the number of hours lost during September was a series of strikes held throughout the month at Peru's only iron miner, Chinese-owned Shougang Hierro Peru S.A, analysts said.

In the first nine months of 1996, Peru lost 1.260 million man-hours in 66 private sector strikes, up from 892,500 hours lost in 81 strikes during the same period last year, the Labor Ministry said in its monthly report.
Peru lost a total 1.049 million man-hours through strikes in 1995, down from 1.937 million in 1994.
The figure has fallen dramatically from the total 15.068 million man-hours lost in 1990 when President Alberto Fujimori's government took power.
